title: Associate Business Analyst Competency Assessment
description: Philippine Skills Framework (PSF-SDS) assessment for Associate Business Analyst.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym SMART stand for when defining project objectives and business requirements?
options: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
Simple, Modern, Agile, Rapid, Tested
Standard, Maintainable, Automated, Robust, Technical
Sequential, Modular, Audited, Reliable, Transparent
questions.correctAnswer: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
questions.explanation: SMART goals ensure clear deliverables with quantifiable targets, achievable timelines, and alignment with business value.

questions.prompt: In Agile Scrum framework, who is solely accountable for maximizing the value of the product and managing the Product Backlog?
options: Product Owner (PO)
Scrum Master
Development Team Lead
Chief Financial Officer
questions.correctAnswer: Product Owner (PO)
questions.explanation: The Product Owner defines backlog user stories, prioritizes features according to business value, and accepts deliverables.

questions.prompt: What is a User Story and what is its standard structure in agile requirements documentation?
options: "As a [type of user], I want [an action/goal] so that [a benefit/value]"
A 500-page technical database schema specification
A legal contract signed by external vendors
A list of employee payroll salaries
questions.correctAnswer: "As a [type of user], I want [an action/goal] so that [a benefit/value]"
questions.explanation: User stories capture requirements from the end-user perspective, focusing on the goal and underlying value proposition.

questions.prompt: In Project Management, what does the "Critical Path" represent?
options: The longest sequence of dependent activities from start to finish that determines the shortest possible project completion duration
The quickest shortcut to deploy code without testing
The path with the lowest financial cost
The list of servers in the computer room
questions.correctAnswer: The longest sequence of dependent activities from start to finish that determines the shortest possible project completion duration
questions.explanation: Any delay on a critical path task directly delays the entire project completion date (zero total float/slack).

questions.prompt: What is a RACI Matrix used for in stakeholder and delivery management?
options: Clarifies roles and responsibilities across activities (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed)
Calculates database query execution time
Estimates software license depreciation costs
Encrypts email passwords
questions.correctAnswer: Clarifies roles and responsibilities across activities (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed)
questions.explanation: RACI matrices prevent role ambiguity and miscommunication by explicitly mapping who does the work and who is accountable.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a Gap Analysis in business analysis?
options: Compares current state (As-Is) with the desired future state (To-Be) to identify gaps, requirements, and required investments
Calculates gaps between desk monitors in an office
Checks for whitespace formatting errors in code
Calculates interest rate inflation
questions.correctAnswer: Compares current state (As-Is) with the desired future state (To-Be) to identify gaps, requirements, and required investments
questions.explanation: Gap analysis illuminates what processes, capabilities, or systems must change to bridge from the present state to the strategic target.

questions.prompt: When two key executive stakeholders have diametrically opposing requirements for a new portal feature, how should the Business Analyst handle it?
options: Facilitate a structured trade-off workshop assessing business impact, strategic alignment, and user data to reach consensus or formal sponsor decision
Secretly implement one stakeholder’s request and hide it from the other
Abandon the project and quit
Vote using a coin toss
questions.correctAnswer: Facilitate a structured trade-off workshop assessing business impact, strategic alignment, and user data to reach consensus or formal sponsor decision
questions.explanation: Objective prioritization workshops evaluate trade-offs, ROI, and alignment transparently to resolve requirement conflicts.

questions.prompt: What is "Scope Creep" in project delivery and how is it controlled?
options: Uncontrolled expansion of project scope without adjustments to time, cost, and resources; controlled through formal Change Request (CR) governance
The sound of cooling fans in data centers
Hiring new employees without HR approval
A type of computer virus
questions.correctAnswer: Uncontrolled expansion of project scope without adjustments to time, cost, and resources; controlled through formal Change Request (CR) governance
questions.explanation: Scope creep causes budget overruns and delays; formal change management ensures any additions are properly evaluated and funded.

questions.prompt: Which metric measures the team’s average amount of work delivered per sprint in Agile Scrum?
options: Velocity (Story Points per sprint)
Burndown Chart
Cycle Time
Lead Time
questions.correctAnswer: Velocity (Story Points per sprint)
questions.explanation: Velocity quantifies the average story points completed per sprint, aiding realistic future capacity forecasting.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Acceptance Criteria in a user story definition?
options: Predefined conditions that a software product must satisfy for the feature to be accepted by the Product Owner and users
The developer’s personal notes
The company dress code policy
A list of external hardware vendors
questions.correctAnswer: Predefined conditions that a software product must satisfy for the feature to be accepted by the Product Owner and users
questions.explanation: Clear acceptance criteria remove ambiguity, defining testable boundaries for Definition of Done (DoD).

questions.prompt: In the context of Associate Business Analyst, when applying "Agile Coaching" (Level 4), what is the most appropriate industry-standard practice?
options: Execute structured, documented protocols aligned with organizational policies, standards, and Level 4 guidelines
Bypass standard change management procedures to finish tasks faster
Delegate all responsibility to junior interns without review
Rely solely on undocumented ad-hoc trial-and-error
questions.correctAnswer: Execute structured, documented protocols aligned with organizational policies, standards, and Level 4 guidelines
questions.explanation: Demonstrating "Agile Coaching" requires adherence to formal methodology, quality standards, and verified procedural frameworks.

questions.prompt: In the context of Associate Business Analyst, when applying "Budgeting" (Level 3), what is the most appropriate industry-standard practice?
options: Execute structured, documented protocols aligned with organizational policies, standards, and Level 3 guidelines
Bypass standard change management procedures to finish tasks faster
Delegate all responsibility to junior interns without review
Rely solely on undocumented ad-hoc trial-and-error
questions.correctAnswer: Execute structured, documented protocols aligned with organizational policies, standards, and Level 3 guidelines
questions.explanation: Demonstrating "Budgeting" requires adherence to formal methodology, quality standards, and verified procedural frameworks.

questions.prompt: In the context of Associate Business Analyst, when applying "Business Agility" (Level 4), what is the most appropriate industry-standard practice?
options: Execute structured, documented protocols aligned with organizational policies, standards, and Level 4 guidelines
Bypass standard change management procedures to finish tasks faster
Delegate all responsibility to junior interns without review
Rely solely on undocumented ad-hoc trial-and-error
questions.correctAnswer: Execute structured, documented protocols aligned with organizational policies, standards, and Level 4 guidelines
questions.explanation: Demonstrating "Business Agility" requires adherence to formal methodology, quality standards, and verified procedural frameworks.

questions.prompt: What does the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) dictate in access control management?

Passwords must be shared in public channels

questions.explanation: Least Privilege minimizes the blast radius of compromised credentials by restricting unnecessary read/write permissions.

questions.prompt: What security vulnerability occurs when an application includes unvalidated user input directly into an SQL command string?
options: SQL Injection (SQLi)
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
Buffer Overflow
questions.correctAnswer: SQL Injection (SQLi)
questions.explanation: SQLi allows attackers to manipulate backend database queries when user input is not parameterized or sanitized.

questions.prompt: Which security header helps protect web applications from Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks by restricting resource origins?
options: Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
Set-Cookie
Cache-Control
Accept-Encoding

questions.explanation: CSP instructs browsers to only execute scripts and load assets from trusted domains, effectively mitigating XSS attacks.

questions.prompt: In asymmetric cryptography, which key is used to decrypt a message that was encrypted using the recipient’s public key?
options: The recipient’s private key
The sender’s public key
The CA root certificate key
A symmetric AES shared key
questions.correctAnswer: The recipient’s private key
questions.explanation: Asymmetric encryption uses key pairs: data encrypted with the public key can only be decrypted by the matching private key.

6 months

Speeds up web page loading by 50%

title: Applications Support Technician Competency Assessment
description: Philippine Skills Framework (PSF-SDS) assessment for Applications Support Technician.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is primarily used for securely logging into remote Linux servers and managing infrastructure over an encrypted channel?
options: Telnet
SSH (Secure Shell, port 22)
FTP (port 21)
HTTP (port 80)
questions.correctAnswer: SSH (Secure Shell, port 22)
questions.explanation: SSH provides strong cryptographic authentication and encrypted communications for remote server administration.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a Reverse Proxy (such as NGINX or HAProxy) in a production web application infrastructure?
options: Acts as the primary database storage engine
Terminates SSL/TLS, distributes client traffic across backend servers, and provides caching and security filtering
Compiles React source code into CSS
Manages DNS domain registrations with ICANN
questions.correctAnswer: Terminates SSL/TLS, distributes client traffic across backend servers, and provides caching and security filtering
questions.explanation: Reverse proxies sit in front of application backends to load-balance traffic, offload SSL termination, and protect internal instances.

questions.prompt: In high-availability database architectures, what is the difference between RPO (Recovery Point Objective) and RTO (Recovery Time Objective)?
options: RPO is the acceptable maximum data loss duration in time; RTO is the acceptable duration to restore operational service
RPO measures network latency; RTO measures disk IOPS
RPO is for cloud backups; RTO is for on-premise tape drives only
There is no difference; both measure server CPU utilization
questions.correctAnswer: RPO is the acceptable maximum data loss duration in time; RTO is the acceptable duration to restore operational service
questions.explanation: RPO focuses on tolerable data loss (how old the recovered data is), while RTO focuses on the maximum allowable downtime.

questions.prompt: A server CPU spikes to 100% and becomes sluggish. Which Linux command suite is most effective to inspect active processes and top resource consumers?
options: top / htop / ps aux
chmod 777
cat /etc/hosts
mkdir -p
questions.correctAnswer: top / htop / ps aux
questions.explanation: top, htop, and ps aux provide real-time process monitoring, memory consumption, CPU breakdown, and PID identification.

questions.prompt: What is the primary function of DNS (Domain Name System)?
options: Translates human-readable domain names (e.g., example.com) into machine IP addresses (e.g., 192.0.2.1)
Encrypts hard drives on server racks
Generates automated SSL certificates
Scans for SQL injection attacks
questions.correctAnswer: Translates human-readable domain names (e.g., example.com) into machine IP addresses (e.g., 192.0.2.1)
questions.explanation: DNS maps human-friendly hostnames to IP addresses so network routers can route packets to the correct endpoints.

questions.prompt: What is Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and what is its primary operational advantage?
options: Writing raw machine assembly for microprocessors
Managing and provisioning compute/storage resources through declarative configuration files, enabling version control and reproducibility
Manually clicking buttons in the cloud provider console
Running daily antivirus scans on virtual machines
questions.correctAnswer: Managing and provisioning compute/storage resources through declarative configuration files, enabling version control and reproducibility
questions.explanation: IaC (e.g., Terraform, Ansible) automates infrastructure provisioning, preventing configuration drift and enabling code review of infra changes.

questions.prompt: In ITIL / Service Level Management, what does an SLA breach typically trigger?
options: Automatic server termination
Incident escalation, penalty calculations (if contractual), and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) review
Immediate deletion of user accounts
Re-installing the operating system
questions.correctAnswer: Incident escalation, penalty calculations (if contractual), and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) review
questions.explanation: Breaching an agreed Service Level Agreement (SLA) requires management notification, prioritization, remediation, and root-cause analysis.

questions.prompt: Which RAID configuration provides disk striping with parity across at least 3 drives, offering both performance and single-drive fault tolerance?
options: RAID 0
RAID 1
RAID 5
JBOD
questions.correctAnswer: RAID 5
questions.explanation: RAID 5 distributes parity across all disks (minimum 3 drives), surviving a single drive failure without losing data.

questions.prompt: During a Sev-1 production outage affecting thousands of users, how should an on-call engineer communicate status updates?
options: Stay silent until the issue is 100% resolved even if it takes 8 hours
Establish an incident bridge, provide periodic factual updates at fixed intervals (e.g., every 15-30 mins), and document timelines clearly
Post on personal social media channels
Blame external network service providers

questions.prompt: What is Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) in test case design?
options: Testing input values at the extreme edges and immediate boundaries of input partitions (e.g. min-1, min, max, max+1)

Measuring how far the mouse cursor moves across the screen
Testing only average random inputs

questions.prompt: When logging a bug report, which components are essential for developers to reproduce and fix it rapidly?

A link to the homepage

questions.prompt: What type of testing ensures that recent code changes or bug fixes have not adversely affected existing functional features?

Stress Testing
Alpha Testing
Penetration Testing

questions.prompt: What is Performance Load Testing vs Stress Testing?

questions.prompt: In an Agile sprint, when should QA testing activities begin?

questions.explanation: Shift-left testing prevents bugs early in user story elaboration, reducing rework and speeding up sprint velocity.

To compress database tables

Ignore all CI/CD pipeline failures permanently
Delete the entire test suite
Blame the cloud provider

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between Black-Box testing and White-Box testing?
options: Black-box tests functionality without knowledge of internal code structure; White-box tests internal code logic and paths
Black-box is for dark mode themes only; White-box is for light mode
Black-box is done after release; White-box is done before planning
There is no difference
questions.correctAnswer: Black-box tests functionality without knowledge of internal code structure; White-box tests internal code logic and paths
questions.explanation: Black-box testing focuses on inputs and expected outputs, whereas white-box testing examines internal branches, statements, and code execution.

questions.prompt: In the Test Automation Pyramid, which layer should contain the highest volume of tests?
options: Unit Tests
Integration Tests
End-to-End (E2E) UI Tests
Manual Exploratory Tests
questions.correctAnswer: Unit Tests
questions.explanation: Unit tests are fast, deterministic, and cheap to maintain, forming the broad base of the test pyramid.

questions.prompt: What is Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) in test case design?
options: Testing input values at the extreme edges and immediate boundaries of input partitions (e.g. min-1, min, max, max+1)
Checking if the database is located in another country
Measuring how far the mouse cursor moves across the screen
Testing only average random inputs
questions.correctAnswer: Testing input values at the extreme edges and immediate boundaries of input partitions (e.g. min-1, min, max, max+1)
questions.explanation: Software defects frequently cluster at boundary transitions (off-by-one errors); BVA systematically targets these edges.

questions.prompt: When logging a bug report, which components are essential for developers to reproduce and fix it rapidly?

Only the word "Broken"
An angry email to the project manager
A link to the homepage
questions.correctAnswer: Title, Clear Step-by-Step Reproduction Steps, Expected Result, Actual Result, Environment Details, and Logs/Screenshots

questions.prompt: What type of testing ensures that recent code changes or bug fixes have not adversely affected existing functional features?

Stress Testing
Alpha Testing
Penetration Testing

questions.prompt: What is Performance Load Testing vs Stress Testing?

Load testing is for CSS; Stress testing is for JavaScript
Both are identical terms
Load testing requires manual clicking only

questions.prompt: In an Agile sprint, when should QA testing activities begin?

Only on the last day of the sprint
After the code is already in production
Never; developers do not need QA in Agile

questions.explanation: Shift-left testing prevents bugs early in user story elaboration, reducing rework and speeding up sprint velocity.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP response code indicates that an API request payload failed validation on the server side?

200 OK
500 Internal Server Error
301 Moved Permanently
questions.correctAnswer: 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity
questions.explanation: 400 and 422 represent client-side validation errors in standard HTTP status code conventions.

To mock and insult other software engineers
To bypass security logins permanently in production
To compress database tables
questions.correctAnswer: To simulate third-party payment gateways or slow downstream APIs without incurring real costs, rate limits, or flakiness
questions.explanation: Mocks simulate external systems reliably so test suites run fast and focus strictly on system-under-test behavior.

Ignore all CI/CD pipeline failures permanently
Delete the entire test suite
Blame the cloud provider
questions.correctAnswer: Quarantine/isolate the test, investigate timing/race conditions or state pollution, fix the root cause, and re-enable it
questions.explanation: Flaky tests erode trust in CI/CD; isolating and diagnosing asynchronous race conditions restores pipeline integrity.

Linked List
Array

questions.explanation: Hash tables use key hashing to achieve O(1) average time complexity for lookups, insertions, and deletions.

questions.prompt: In RESTful API design, which HTTP method should be used to apply partial modifications to an existing resource?
options: PUT
POST
PATCH
UPDATE
questions.correctAnswer: PATCH
questions.explanation: PATCH is intended for partial modifications of a resource, whereas PUT replaces the entire resource representation.

questions.prompt: What is the primary benefit of adhering to the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) in software design?
options: Increases application execution speed
Ensures a class has only one reason to change, improving maintainability and testability
Reduces the number of files in the codebase
Enables automatic database query caching
questions.correctAnswer: Ensures a class has only one reason to change, improving maintainability and testability
questions.explanation: SRP ensures each module or class encapsulates a single responsibility, isolating changes and reducing regression risks.

questions.prompt: When designing a microservices architecture, which pattern is recommended to ensure data consistency across multiple services without distributed locks?
options: Two-Phase Commit (2PC)
Saga Pattern
Active-Passive Replication
Shared Database Pattern
questions.correctAnswer: Saga Pattern
questions.explanation: The Saga Pattern manages distributed transactions via a sequence of local transactions coordinated through events or choreography.

questions.prompt: In asynchronous programming, what problem does a thread pool prevent when handling high-concurrency I/O workloads?
options: Memory leaks in garbage collection
Thread creation overhead and resource exhaustion from unbounded thread spawning
SQL injection vulnerabilities
Network packet fragmentation
questions.correctAnswer: Thread creation overhead and resource exhaustion from unbounded thread spawning
questions.explanation: Thread pools reuse existing worker threads, avoiding the steep CPU and memory overhead of creating and destroying OS threads.

questions.prompt: Which Git command allows you to selectively apply a specific commit from one branch onto another without merging the whole branch?
options: git rebase -i
git cherry-pick
git merge --squash
git pull --rebase
questions.correctAnswer: git cherry-pick
questions.explanation: git cherry-pick applies the changes introduced by one or more specific commits onto the current HEAD branch.

questions.prompt: You discover a memory leak in a production Node.js/Go service under sustained traffic. What is the most methodical first step to diagnose it?
options: Immediately restart the servers every hour using a cron job
Capture heap snapshots over time under load and analyze object retention graphs
Disable all database indexing
Rewrite the service in another programming language
questions.correctAnswer: Capture heap snapshots over time under load and analyze object retention graphs
questions.explanation: Comparing heap snapshots highlights growing retained memory and uncollected references causing the memory leak.

questions.prompt: How does Dependency Injection (DI) support unit testing?
options: It compiles code into machine bytecode faster
It allows mocking or stubbing external dependencies (e.g. database, HTTP clients) cleanly
It eliminates the need for test assertions
It automatically writes regression test suites
questions.correctAnswer: It allows mocking or stubbing external dependencies (e.g. database, HTTP clients) cleanly
questions.explanation: DI passes dependencies into components, enabling test suites to supply mock implementations without touching production infrastructure.

questions.prompt: In relational databases, what does an index scan on a B-Tree structure provide compared to a full table scan?
options: Logarithmic O(log N) lookup time for filtered queries instead of linear O(N) full scan
Compression of all audio and video assets
Zero disk write overhead during INSERT operations
Automatic cross-region data replication
questions.correctAnswer: Logarithmic O(log N) lookup time for filtered queries instead of linear O(N) full scan
questions.explanation: B-Tree indexes enable database engines to traverse sorted tree nodes in O(log N) operations to retrieve matching rows quickly.

Convene the release lead, QA, and engineering team to evaluate risk, scope a hotfix or rollback contingency, and communicate transparently to stakeholders

Cancel the entire product indefinitely

questions.prompt: According to WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility guidelines, what is the minimum required contrast ratio for normal body text against its background?
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.1 AA requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text (and 3:1 for large text 18pt+).

questions.prompt: In UX research, what is the primary purpose of an A/B test?
options: To test if the server can handle 10,000 concurrent database writes
To compare two versions of a design against a measurable conversion metric with randomized user cohorts
To design the company brand typography from scratch
To write automated CSS unit tests
questions.correctAnswer: To compare two versions of a design against a measurable conversion metric with randomized user cohorts
questions.explanation: A/B testing evaluates hypothesis variations by splitting traffic to identify which design yields statistically significant engagement.

questions.prompt: What is the main goal of establishing a Design System (with Design Tokens, Component Libraries, and Guidelines)?
options: Ensure consistency across product surfaces, speed up design-to-development handoff, and enable scalable UI updates
Eliminate the need for frontend software engineers
Store candidate resumes in SQL databases
Replace user research with automated AI scripts
questions.correctAnswer: Ensure consistency across product surfaces, speed up design-to-development handoff, and enable scalable UI updates
questions.explanation: Design systems enforce brand and usability consistency while accelerating delivery through reusable components and tokens.

questions.prompt: Which usability evaluation method involves having evaluators inspect an interface against established design principles (e.g., Nielsen’s 10 Heuristics)?
options: Heuristic Evaluation
Card Sorting
Tree Testing
Eye-tracking heatmap study
questions.correctAnswer: Heuristic Evaluation
questions.explanation: Heuristic evaluation involves expert reviewers assessing a UI against recognized usability principles to discover UX friction.

questions.prompt: What is Fitts’s Law and how does it influence UI button placement and size?
options: The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target; larger, closer buttons are faster and easier to click
Users read websites in a Z-pattern only
Dark mode always consumes 50% less battery
All mobile screens must have exactly 5 navigation tabs
questions.correctAnswer: The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target; larger, closer buttons are faster and easier to click
questions.explanation: Fitts’s Law models human movement: critical interactive targets should have adequate touch target sizing (e.g. 44x44px) and reachable placement.

questions.prompt: When writing UX microcopy for a destructive action (such as deleting a project), which button label adheres best to clarity guidelines?
options: OK
Yes / No
Delete Project
Submit
questions.correctAnswer: Delete Project
questions.explanation: Specific, action-oriented button copy (e.g., "Delete Project") makes the consequence explicit and prevents accidental data loss.

questions.prompt: In the Double Diamond design framework, what are the four phases?
options: Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver
Code, Compile, Test, Deploy
Plan, Budget, Spend, Audit
Input, Process, Output, Storage
questions.correctAnswer: Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver
questions.explanation: The British Design Council’s Double Diamond uses divergent and convergent thinking across Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver.

questions.prompt: When presenting design prototypes to engineering and product stakeholders who have conflicting opinions, what is the best strategy?
options: Ignore all feedback and build your own preference
Anchor decisions in user research data, business goals, and technical feasibility constraints, explaining the trade-offs clearly
Stop the project immediately
Ask the engineers to redesign the prototype
questions.correctAnswer: Anchor decisions in user research data, business goals, and technical feasibility constraints, explaining the trade-offs clearly
questions.explanation: Grounding design walkthroughs in user data and objective requirements turns subjective debates into constructive problem-solving.

questions.prompt: What UX research methodology is best suited for understanding how users naturally categorize and structure information in an app menu?
options: Card Sorting
5-Second Test
System Usability Scale (SUS) survey
A/B Test
questions.correctAnswer: Card Sorting
questions.explanation: Card sorting allows participants to organize topics into logical groups, informing intuitive information architecture and navigation.

To guide and educate users on what will appear once data is present, providing a clear call-to-action to get started
To crash the browser tab safely
To force the user to log out
questions.correctAnswer: To guide and educate users on what will appear once data is present, providing a clear call-to-action to get started
questions.explanation: Thoughtful empty states prevent user confusion, provide helpful onboarding guidance, and prompt actionable next steps.

title: User Interface (UI) Designer Competency Assessment
description: Philippine Skills Framework (PSF-SDS) assessment for User Interface (UI) Designers covering accessibility, responsive layouts, design systems, and micro-interactions.

questions.prompt: When designing a data-dense dashboard, which typography technique best establishes a clear visual hierarchy without cluttering the screen?
options: Use 6 different font families to distinguish sections.
Use a single versatile font family with systematic variations in font weight, size scale, and muted color contrast (e.g., 600 weight for headers, 400 for body, neutral-500 for secondary metadata).
Set all text in UPPERCASE bold with high saturation colors.
Use italicized serif fonts for all numeric data.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a single versatile font family with systematic variations in font weight, size scale, and muted color contrast (e.g., 600 weight for headers, 400 for body, neutral-500 for secondary metadata).
questions.explanation: A constrained typographic scale with varying weights and subtle contrast creates strong scanning anchors without visual noise.

questions.prompt: According to WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance, what is the minimum required color contrast ratio between regular body text (under 18pt) and its background?
questions.explanation: WCAG AA mandates at least 4.5:1 for regular text and 3:1 for large text (18pt+ or 14pt bold).

questions.prompt: When transitioning a multi-column desktop data table to a mobile screen (under 480px), which UI design pattern delivers the best user experience?
options: Shrink the font size to 6px so all 10 columns fit on one screen.
Transform table rows into stacked cards showing key summary metrics with an expandable drawer for full details.
Hide all columns except the ID column.
Disable mobile access and show an error banner.
questions.correctAnswer: Transform table rows into stacked cards showing key summary metrics with an expandable drawer for full details.
questions.explanation: Card transformation preserves content legibility and touch-friendly targets on narrow viewports.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of utilizing Design Tokens (e.g., color-primary-500, spacing-4, radius-md) in a cross-platform design system?
options: To replace JavaScript logic in web browsers.
To store centralized design decisions as platform-agnostic key-value pairs that sync automatically between Figma and codebase stylesheets.
To compress SVG icon file sizes.
To encrypt confidential user interface assets.
questions.correctAnswer: To store centralized design decisions as platform-agnostic key-value pairs that sync automatically between Figma and codebase stylesheets.
questions.explanation: Design tokens serve as the single source of truth for design decisions across web, iOS, and Android platforms.

questions.prompt: According to Fitts’s Law, which placement and sizing strategy makes a primary "Submit Application" button easiest and fastest to activate on mobile?
options: A 20x20px floating icon at the top-left corner of the screen.
A full-width bottom sticky action bar with a minimum 44px touch target height placed within natural thumb reach.
A tiny hyperlink hidden inside the footer copyright notice.
Placing the button in a multi-level hover dropdown menu.
questions.correctAnswer: A full-width bottom sticky action bar with a minimum 44px touch target height placed within natural thumb reach.
questions.explanation: Fitts's Law states target acquisition speed depends on distance and size. Bottom-anchored large targets are fastest to reach with thumbs.

questions.prompt: When a user clicks a button that triggers a 3-second backend API request, what is the best UI state feedback?
options: Keep the button static with no change and let the user wait.
Change the button to a disabled state showing an inline animated spinner with "Processing..." text, while keeping button dimensions constant to prevent layout shift.
Clear the entire screen immediately to a blank white page.
Show a pop-up alert box on every mouse movement.
questions.correctAnswer: Change the button to a disabled state showing an inline animated spinner with "Processing..." text, while keeping button dimensions constant to prevent layout shift.
questions.explanation: Instant visual feedback informs the user that their request is executing and prevents accidental double-submissions.

questions.prompt: What constitutes an effective "Empty State" for a new recruiter who has 0 active job postings?
options: A blank white box that says "404 No Data Found".
An illustrative graphic, a friendly explanation of why the list is empty, and a prominent primary button: "+ Create Your First Job Posting".
Automatically log out the user.
Display fake dummy data without informing the user.
questions.correctAnswer: An illustrative graphic, a friendly explanation of why the list is empty, and a prominent primary button: "+ Create Your First Job Posting".
questions.explanation: Effective empty states educate users, provide context, and guide them with a clear call-to-action (CTA).

questions.prompt: Where and when should form validation errors (such as an invalid email format) be communicated to the user?
options: In an unformatted JavaScript alert() popup after clicking submit 3 times.
Inline directly beneath the specific input field, triggered on blur or during submission, with clear instructional text and a distinct error color/icon.
At the very bottom of the website footer.
Only sent via email 24 hours later.
questions.correctAnswer: Inline directly beneath the specific input field, triggered on blur or during submission, with clear instructional text and a distinct error color/icon.
questions.explanation: Inline field validation provides immediate spatial context, allowing users to correct mistakes effortlessly.

questions.prompt: When designing a Dark Mode theme for a dashboard, what is the recommended practice for background surfaces?
options: Use pure #000000 for all backgrounds with pure #FFFFFF for all text.
Use layered dark gray surfaces (e.g., #121212 for base, #1E1E1E for elevated cards) to convey elevation and reduce harsh eye strain.
Invert all colors automatically using a CSS invert(100%) filter.
Make all images transparent.
questions.correctAnswer: Use layered dark gray surfaces (e.g., #121212 for base, #1E1E1E for elevated cards) to convey elevation and reduce harsh eye strain.
questions.explanation: Dark surfaces with varying luminance indicate elevation and shadows while preventing high-contrast glare.

questions.prompt: What is the ideal duration for standard UI micro-animations (such as modal fade-ins, tooltip popups, or tab transitions)?
options: 2000ms – 3000ms (2–3 seconds)
150ms – 300ms (0.15–0.3 seconds) with ease-out or ease-in-out curves
10ms (instantaneous flicker)
10,000ms (10 seconds)
questions.correctAnswer: 150ms – 300ms (0.15–0.3 seconds) with ease-out or ease-in-out curves
questions.explanation: 150ms–300ms is fast enough to feel responsive while smooth enough for the human eye to track state transitions.

questions.prompt: In an application with over 15 distinct functional modules, what navigation structure minimizes cognitive overload for daily users?
options: Display all 15 links horizontally across the top navbar in 9px text.
A collapsible sidebar grouping related features under categorized sections (e.g., "Main Menu", "Hiring Pipeline", "Settings") with recognizable icons and active indicators.
Hide all navigation inside a 5-step nested right-click context menu.
Require users to type URL routes manually.
questions.correctAnswer: A collapsible sidebar grouping related features under categorized sections (e.g., "Main Menu", "Hiring Pipeline", "Settings") with recognizable icons and active indicators.
questions.explanation: Categorized sidebar navigation establishes mental models and keeps primary workflows easily accessible.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best exemplifies Nielsen’s heuristic: "Recognition rather than recall"?
options: Forcing the user to memorize product IDs from page 1 and type them on page 5.
Showing recent search queries, auto-complete suggestions, and visual thumbnails so users don't have to remember details from memory.
Hiding password requirements until the form fails 5 times.
Disabling browser back buttons.
questions.correctAnswer: Showing recent search queries, auto-complete suggestions, and visual thumbnails so users don't have to remember details from memory.
questions.explanation: Making options and actions visible reduces mental cognitive load.

questions.prompt: Why should standalone navigation icons almost always be accompanied by text labels or accessible tooltips?
options: Icons without labels often suffer from ambiguous meaning across different cultures and user groups.
Web browsers cannot render SVG images alone.
Search engines penalize websites that have icons.
Text labels speed up internet network bandwidth.
questions.correctAnswer: Icons without labels often suffer from ambiguous meaning across different cultures and user groups.
questions.explanation: Abstract icons can be misinterpreted; combining icons with text labels maximizes clarity and accessibility.

questions.prompt: During UI design handoff to software engineers, which artifact is most critical to ensure pixel-accurate and bug-free implementation?
options: A flat JPEG screenshot with no specifications.
A specification with component states (default, hover, active, focus, disabled, loading), responsive breakpoints, spacing tokens, and asset exports.
A 50-page printed physical PDF.
Asking the engineer to guess the margin and padding values.
questions.correctAnswer: A specification with component states (default, hover, active, focus, disabled, loading), responsive breakpoints, spacing tokens, and asset exports.
questions.explanation: Documenting state variations and layout tokens eliminates implementation discrepancies during development.

questions.prompt: Which practice is considered a deceptive "Dark Pattern" that a professional UI designer should actively avoid?
options: Highlighting the recommended pricing tier with a subtle badge.
"Confirmshaming" — using manipulative copy like "No thanks, I hate saving money" on opt-out buttons to guilt-trip users into signing up.
Providing keyboard shortcuts for power users.
Offering a dark mode toggle.
questions.correctAnswer: "Confirmshaming" — using manipulative copy like "No thanks, I hate saving money" on opt-out buttons to guilt-trip users into signing up.
questions.explanation: Dark patterns manipulate user psychology through deceptive copy or misleading visual hierarchies, undermining user trust.
